memory_update.text: PWR should remain the reference benchmark for grid infrastructure backlog and skilled craft-labor constraints, but should not dominate the underfollowed lane.

MYRG is a priority underfollowed contractor candidate for utility T&D and electrical infrastructure execution capacity; next layer should separate utility-linked backlog from cyclical commercial construction.
POWL is a priority equipment chokepoint candidate because backlog and utility awards suggest exposure to scarce engineered electrical distribution/control systems.

NVEE is a priority permitting, inspection, conformity assessment, and public-works administration candidate; evidence strength depends on verifying public/quasi-public revenue mix and backlog quality.

Election-sensitive infrastructure research should track already-funded or hard-to-reverse programs: grid reliability, utility T&D, public works, permitting/code enforcement, environmental compliance, and inspection capacity.

Security and border-infrastructure equipment suppliers such as inspection/scanning vendors remain a gap for a later pass; OSI Systems surfaced as a possible lead but was excluded here to keep the list capped at four and grid/permitting-focused.

node: Election-sensitive public spending infrastructure: grid, security, permitting, and public works
summary: Layer 1B expands the node around scarce infrastructure capacity rather than direct election outcomes. The highest-signal public-market mapping is not the obvious policy headline, but the constrained execution layer: grid construction labor, substation and electrical distribution equipment, permitting/code-inspection capacity, and utility/public-sector engineering services. One reference leader is included for context, while the discovery lane emphasizes smaller or less-followed firms with backlog, utility/public-sector exposure, or narrow chokepoint roles.
